messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed ~10% spike in streaming disconnects on the EU canary around 22:15 UTC. Dashboard churn up but trace sampling stayed at 0.5%. /cc @vikram
vikram: Which route/pool? sticky routing enabled? Any proxy 5xxs in logs?
jordan: We pushed the proxy-rebalancer canary ~21:50 with 5% weight for ws-eu-prod-canary. No other infra deploys AFAIK.
maria: Route is ws-eu-prod-canary. Quick log snippet from the edge: `ERROR stream: upstream reset (code=502) conn_id=abcd1234`
amelia: Console shows resume attempts doubled at the same time, but billing shows no duplicate token charges. Telemetry mismatch — sampling might be filtering out deploy metadata.
deploy-bot: deploy: proxy-rebalancer canary @jordan succeeded (21:50 UTC) :rocket:
vikram: Could be resume token auth change or keepalive header? If proxy starts returning 5xx on attach we may be force-closing before session tombstone. Can we get a raw client/server capture? 
maria: Grabbed a client-side trace. SDK is setting `reconnectBackoffMs = 0` for some test builds. Snippet: ```js
// test harness override
client.options.reconnectBackoffMs = 0
```
jordan: Ugh that's an accidental default from the mobile test harness. Should be gated by a header flag. If clients reconnect immediately we get thundering on a small canary pool.
amelia: Also saw resume attempts, but the console tracing filter removed the deploy tag so traces didn't show canary route. I'll fix sampling.
ops: Collected pcap + proxy logs. Server shows repeated `upstream reset` then `session closed by server (hard)` within <500ms of attach. Path: /var/log/proxy/ws-edge.log (uploaded to the incident bucket).
vikram: Hypothesis: canary routes hit smaller upstream set -> a transient upstream reset causes immediate hard close by proxy -> clients reconnect with 0 backoff -> reconnect storm. Short-term mitigations: 1) add jitter/positive backoff in SDK; 2) make proxy use soft-close + keep tombstone for 30s before hard close to allow client resume.
maria: I agree on SDK jitter. Also request a console UX change: overlay route weight + deploy tag on the streaming disconnect graph. Right now you can't correlate weight vs disconnect spikes.
jordan: We discussed overlay in the last retro — should be quick: add timeseries for route_weight and a deploy_tag annotation layer. I'll open a spike.
amelia: I'll open dashboard PR and also rollback the proxy-rebalancer canary until we push fixes. cc @ops
amelia: filing rollback now :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback: proxy-rebalancer canary @jordan triggered (22:28 UTC) :warning:
maria: Let's not fire a full incident yet — this is canary-scoped. I'll pin this thread and add an alert rule to trigger if disconnect rate >5% across >2 regions.
vikram: Sounds good. After rollback we should instrument a synthetic client with randomized backoff to validate. Also add route-weight to telemetry ingestion so queries can join easily.
jordan: I'll follow up with a tiny SDK patch to ensure default backoff >= 250ms and jitter. Will also add a deploy-gate header so tests don't flip it.
amelia: Thanks all. I'll update the dashboard PR link here once ready and attach the log bundle.
ops: log bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-infra/incident/1757772222/proxy-logs.tar.gz
maria: Thanks. Assigning owners: console overlay -> @amelia, SDK backoff -> @jordan, proxy soft-close TTL -> @vikram. Will re-open thread if we see further anomalies.
